summary: @servicetitan/cp-api preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute opaque obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (v1.3.13), extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a shipped `math_init.js` file — falling back to a system `bun` if one is already installed. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` payload with a rotating string-array decoder (`WV8StW` shifting a >1000-entry constant table) and mangled identifiers, executed only under the fetched Bun runtime so Node-based analysis never evaluates it. The advertised library surface in `dist/` is a trivial re-export of three axios helper files, entirely disconnected from the preinstall behavior. Fetching a second language runtime at install time solely to execute an obfuscated sibling file under it is not a legitimate build pattern for an npm API-client library; the split-runtime delivery and heavy obfuscation prevent audit of the executed code before it runs on the installer's machine. The package name additionally sits in the vendor-branded `@servicetitan/*` scope while shipping content inconsistent with a ServiceTitan API client, consistent with scope masquerading.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
